Senses.Explanation: The expression denotes one-finger Chan in these Chan records. Its wording is "one-finger Chan." The phrase names Juzhi's recorded use of a raised finger in public interviews. A later record states the visible rule directly: "Whenever someone came, Master Juzhi only extended one finger; he called it one-finger Chan" (俱胝和尚逢人但伸一指頭，喚做一指頭禪). In the transmitted case, Tianlong raises one finger to Juzhi; afterward, whenever students ask, Juzhi raises one finger, and before dying he says, "I obtained Tianlong's one-finger Chan; through my whole life I could not use it up" (吾得天龍一指頭禪，一生用不盡). The record also preserves criticism rather than making the label an unquestioned formula: Xuansha says he would have broken the finger, Caoshan faults Juzhi's taking it up, and Sanshan asks, "What connection does one-finger Chan have? It cheated that monk and buried him alive his whole life" (一指頭禪有甚交涉？賺殺阿僧終身活埋). Its Chan-specific bend is thus a named, publicly repeated response inherited from Tianlong and continually examined by later masters.
